title: Influence of “motivational interviewing” on the dental and general health of children and their parents
summary:
Caries is still a relevant problem for children in Germany - every second child aged six is affected. Many of these children have to be treated under general anaesthesia for severe tooth decay. However, international studies show that many children quickly develop tooth decay again after such treatment.
A key factor in children's dental health is the behaviour of their parents, particularly with regard to dental care and diet. Traditional advice and information brochures often have little success because they rarely lead to a lasting change in behaviour.
A new, promising approach is motivational interviewing (MI). This is a special form of counselling in which parents are actively involved and, together with the counsellor, set goals for a healthier lifestyle for their children. These conversations are designed to strengthen the inner motivation to change rather than just giving instructions.

This study investigates whether MI can help families with caries-active children to improve nutritional and dental care behaviour in the long term. All participating children are first treated for caries under general anaesthesia. Their parents then receive either regular motivational talks or the usual information on dental health.
The aim is to test whether MI is better at preventing the progression of early childhood caries than conventional counselling. Further points are: How often parents take their children for follow-up check-ups, whether inflammation levels in the mouth improve, how parents' knowledge and behaviour changes - and what possible reasons there were for previous problems with dental care.
In the long term, the study should help to sustainably improve children's dental health - especially in families that have previously had little access to effective support.

interventions.name: Children and their parents who are referred to the paediatric dentistry department at Dresden University Hospital for early childhood caries therapy under general anaesthesia are examined. The study group receives a 30-minute motivational interview (MI) at the start of therapy to improve nutrition a

The control group also consists of patients who are referred for caries treatment under general anaesthesia. In this group, the parents do not receive an MI discussion but conventional health instruction as part of FU1a-b or FU2.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Children with early childhood caries (ECC), age 2-6 years
- Children with non-compliance for caries therapy under local anaesthetic
- Parents or legal guardians of the above-mentioned children
Exclusion criteria:
- General illnesses
- Regular intake of medication
- The legal guardians do not have sufficient knowledge of German to be informed about the treatment and the study procedure without an interpreter
